record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked documentation were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a domain-specific weight-editing workflow based on the cited contrastive weight-editing approach and reports its own synthetic reference experiment. That experiment measures a fictional restriction task, not safety refusal.
record.gate_note: The reported reference experiment uses a fictional museum restriction and explicitly says it does not establish anything about general safety behavior. Its target-marker and control-answer results are retained as findings about this synthetic task, not as tests of the listed safety-refusal versions. Other numerical details, such as memory estimates, are not experiment outcomes.
record.test_reason: This is a tool repository built on the Arditi et al. contrastive weight edit. Its only reported run targets a fictional museum-archive restriction that the system prompt itself imposes, scored by a restriction marker. That is a behaviour induced on purpose by instructions, not safety refusal arising from training. The README says it does not establish anything about general safety behaviour. No result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The run verified the GPU editing and checkpoint-reload pipeline, but the edit failed to remove the fictional target restriction and damaged controls. The authors state that the synthetic task does not establish anything about general safety behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a contrastive weight edit based on the original work, using domain-specific target/control prompts and a residual-writing weight projection rather than reporting the original harmful-versus-harmless activation intervention. This is a tool/workflow repository.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen3-0.6B, a contrastive residual-projection weight edit aimed at a system-prompt-imposed fictional restriction left the held-out target marker rate at 100%. Control answer-match fell from 98.3% to 36.7% (120 test prompts).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means weight edit may fail to remove an instruction-induced, domain-specific restriction behaviour while damaging control answers, in a small model.

record.problems: The only reported run uses one model and a fictional restriction task rather than real safety refusals. The README gives no uncertainty values for the reported rates, and the edit substantially damages control answer matching.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible experiment-result rows were stated in the README. Other run artifacts are described as outputs but are not bundled in the repository listing.

untested.parts: No harmful-vs-harmless direction, ablation or addition on safety refusal.
The weight edit was applied only to an instructed fictional restriction, not to refusal in a safety-trained model. The workflow figure caption's claim about removing safeguards has no reported data.
No comparison of one direction against several.
No reasoning-model result. Qwen3-0.6B has a thinking mode, but it is not analysed.

missing.what: Full reference-run measurements, including the group-bootstrap intervals and validation sweep the README says are reported. These are not read; they would supply uncertainty for r1 and r2.

record.verdict_notes: Single run, single 0.6B model, no uncertainty in the README. The restriction is defined in the system file with a marker, so it is an induced behaviour, a further reason it falls outside the claim. The workflow image caption asserts that abliteration can remove refusal safeguards, but no supporting result is given. Linked docs and code were not read.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-versus-harmless refusal test or activation ablation/addition result is reported.
The reference weight edit targets a fictional restriction behavior, not refusal in a safety-trained model.
No jailbreak suppression or adversarial training result is reported.
No comparison of one direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal-decision representation is measured.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer result is reported.
No reasoning-model refusal result is reported.
